slot_note: re-rooted twice in Batch 3: architecture 1 (Hospital in the Home, healthcare-delivery) closed at the queue reset; architecture 2 (district heating design-day flow, energy-systems-utilities) spent at stage 4 when two judges found its comparison group identifiable only by its outcome; energy, healthcare and physical-environmental sciences are banned by the last three builds, so the slot moves to Sociology & Demography with a new world, dataset, generator and shell, objective kept (Forecasting)
niche: a Dutch school board forecasting whether its primary school De Kwikstaart outgrows its buildings' capacity on the 1 October counts of 2027 to 2029, each child of the catchment counted at the share of the last five intakes' children in the same circumstance (a brother or sister from the same household on the school's roll at the child's first count, or not), the circumstance found by joining the population register's households to the school's roll, which share no key
analyst_test: A strong planner who reads PV-2 and the accommodation plan and forecasts the catchment's entrants at the school's pooled share of the last five intakes (48 per cent), at that share by neighbourhood or on its trend, files that De Kwikstaart stays within its 604 pupils through 2029-30 (none), when the coming cohorts hold several times the past intakes' share of children with a brother or sister on the roll, who enter at 97 per cent against 43, and the school is short at the 2029-30 count.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the expected intake of each coming school year, each child of the catchment counted at the entry rate of the last intakes' children in the same circumstance, the demographer's cohort projection of a school roll; with another field's nouns there is no cohort that first counts at four, no household whose older child on the roll draws the younger one in, and no roll that ages through eight groups.
layer1: the population register's dates in dd-mm-yyyy and the school's roll in ISO dates, the roll's postcodes without the space
house-number additions typed differently in the register (huisletter A, 1) and the roll (a, -1)
residence periods in the register (datum_adres, datum_vertrek): households that left the district during the five intakes
the school's pupil administration replaced in August 2023: four-digit pupil numbers until the 2022 count, KW numbers from 2023
the grid operator's EAN re-registration and meter exchanges at the school's two gas connections, one resent read
the after-school care provider's family rows carrying a number of children, and its location re-coded at a merger on 12 October 2026
stakeholder_role: the school board's director of operations, who signs the board's accommodation request to the municipality

spine.entity: one resident of the district at one address

world.geography: Netherlands (a fictional city, its school board, a primary school and a childcare provider; all names invented)

driver: Newcomers join a unit at a rate that depends on whether a related member is already inside, a relation no field records and only the household register joined to the roll reveals; carrying the newcomers at the unit's pooled share of past cohorts, or at that share by area or on its trend, misses that the coming cohorts hold several times the related share of the past ones.
driver_concrete: Each catchment child who first counts in 2027 to 2029 enters at the share of the last five intakes' children in its circumstance (97 per cent with a brother or sister from the same household on the roll, 43 without, read by joining the register's households to the roll by birth date and address), and the coming cohorts hold 34 per cent with such a sibling against 9 in the past intakes, so the school's 604 places are exceeded at the 2029-30 count, not never as the pooled 48 per cent, the neighbourhood shares or the trend file.
stump: A competent planner forecasts the entrants at the school's pooled share of the last five intakes, by neighbourhood or on its trend, and files that the school stays within its capacity through 2029-30; the step that lands it there is pooling children whose entry rate depends on a brother or sister on the roll, when the coming cohorts carry several times the past share of such children and the school is short at the 2029-30 count.

lineage.niche: a purchasing alliance of five Victorian public health services booking a private nursing provider's January to March 2027 Hospital in the Home overflow block, each member topped up in the alliance agreement's order to its 90th-percentile HITH visit requirement above its in-house nurses' capacity, when two members open a bone and joint infection at home pathway whose courses run for weeks
lineage.driver: The upper percentile of a period's total is set by how many of the units that generate it arrive and how long each one runs, so it has to be built from those units and their durations counted inside the window; treating the counted rows, or the weeks or months they fall in, as independent draws, or carrying a site's own past spread onto a planned mix that adds long-running units, understates it and misplaces every capped top-up.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each member's January to March 2027 HITH visits are the home days of patients admitted at random, each stream's stay set by its course (weeks for a bone and joint infection, days for cellulitis), so the 90th-percentile requirement is built from the plan's admissions by stream and the stays on file counted inside the quarter; a Poisson margin on the planned visits, or the spread of past weeks, months or quarters carried onto the plan, understates it, most at the two members opening the bone and joint infection pathway, and books the block in the wrong lots.
lineage.stump: A competent solver takes each member's planned visits as its expected requirement, adds the 90th-percentile margin of a Poisson count (or the spread of its past monthly visits) and books small lots spread across all five members; the step that lands it there is treating visits as independent counts when they arrive in admissions whose stays run from days to weeks, so the quarter's spread is the admissions' and their stays': built from them, the two pathway members need several lots each and the block runs out before the last member in the order.
lineage.answer: Northgate Health books 300 visits, Riverbend Health 250, Westmere Health 225, Kingsdale Health 75 and Hillcrest Health none: the 850-visit block runs out at Kingsdale
lineage.world: Australia, Victoria: Ironbark Health Alliance, Bellbird Home Nursing (Hospital in the Home overflow block)
lineage.fate: re-rooted 2026-11-01 at the Batch 3 queue reset: shipped 2026-10-15 with no portal result; one architecture per world, so the Hospital in the Home world is closed and the slot moves to another client domain

lineage.niche: a Dutch city's district heating company deciding in which heating season its west network's pump station first runs short on a design day once a housing corporation's 1970s flats leave their block gas boilers for the heat network in six phases across 2027 and 2028, each block's design-day circulation flow its design heat load over the temperature drop that connections heated by the same kind of installation make on cold days
lineage.driver: A newcomer's draw on a shared carrier is its load over the drop it makes in the carrier, and the drop belongs to the equipment behind it, which the units already on the carrier show only as two regimes in their own readings that no field labels; carrying the newcomers at the carrier's design drop, its measured average or the average of similar-looking units finds room that is not there.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each converting block's design-day flow is its design heat load over 1.163 times the supply-return drop that the network's connections with original radiator systems make on days at or below 0 C (about 24 K, readable only as the high-return regime in the heat meters), not the network's 40 K design drop, its metered cold-day drop of 39.7 K or the pre-1985 buildings' 33 to 42 K, so OS West runs short in the 2028-29 season instead of never; a textbook 90/70 radiator drop of 20 K files 2027-28.
lineage.stump: A competent planner converts each block's design heat load into flow at the network's 40 K design drop, its metered cold-day drop or the pre-1985 buildings' drop and files that OS West never runs short through 2028-29; the step that lands it there is carrying blocks that keep their original radiators at a drop those radiators cannot make, when the network's own radiator connections, recognisable only by their high returns, run at about 24 K on cold days and put the station short in 2028-29.
lineage.answer: 2028-29 heating season (phases 1 to 6 need about 200 m3/h of design-day flow against 168 available at OS West, short by about 30; 2027-28 holds at about 150)

spine.entity: one heat meter's reading for one UTC day

differentiation.task140: task140 solves a compute pool's lowest-tier residual jointly with a dependent service whose load rises with that tier; task142 has no residual or dependency: each unmetered block's design-day flow is its load over the drop of its own installation, read from the metered connections whose cold-day returns show that installation, and the shared axes (objective gap, a unit swap, a capacity report) carry different mechanisms
differentiation.task134: task134 raises a held level's forward rate by the distance the untouched ground beside it shows; task142 has no held level or rate: it converts kilowatts to cubic metres an hour through a physical drop read from like installations on the same network
differentiation.task133: task133 lets each truck rise to the next binding limit in another dimension; task142 has no second limit: the one capacity is the station's flow, and the decisive estimate is the drop the unmetered blocks' radiators will make
differentiation.task167: task167 v2 matches a young grant book to the units whose first-year draws looked like its own and reads their schedule at later ages; task142's newcomers have no record at all: the blocks are unmetered, their installation is known from the works, and the parameter is a physical drop read from the metered connections whose cold-day returns form the high-return regime, with no age or schedule
differentiation.task261: task261 recomputes a subgroup difference's standard error over a design's replicates; task142 estimates no variance and compares no subgroups: it forecasts a station's design-day flow from a drop read off like installations
differentiation.task149: task149 v2 turns a census workplace tally into weekly trips at each workplace's own travel frequency read from a panel of workers' stays; task142 counts no trips and reads no panel: it converts unmetered blocks' kilowatts to cubic metres an hour through the drop of the metered connections that share their radiator installation
